events.title: Birth of Joan of Arc (traditional date)
events.description: Joan of Arc, the French peasant girl who would lead French forces during the Hundred Years' War, is traditionally said to have been born on this date in Domrémy, France. The exact date is uncertain and rests on a later tradition.
events.significance: Joan of Arc became a national heroine of France and a Catholic saint. Her military leadership, especially the relief of Orléans in 1429, helped turn the tide of the Hundred Years' War.

events.title: First Public Demonstration of the Telegraph
events.description: Samuel Morse and Alfred Vail gave the first public demonstration of their telegraph system at the Speedwell Ironworks in Morristown, New Jersey, transmitting a message over two miles of wire using their code.
events.significance: The demonstration paved the way for long-distance electrical communication. Morse code and the telegraph transformed commerce, journalism, and military operations around the world.

events.title: New Mexico Admitted as the 47th U.S. State
events.description: President William Howard Taft signed the proclamation admitting New Mexico to the Union as the 47th state, ending decades as a territory following the Mexican-American War.
events.significance: Statehood gave New Mexico full representation in the federal government and recognized its distinct Hispanic, Native American, and Anglo cultural heritage.

events.title: Roosevelt's Four Freedoms Speech
events.description: In his State of the Union address, President Franklin D. Roosevelt outlined four fundamental freedoms: freedom of speech, freedom of worship, freedom from want, and freedom from fear.
events.significance: The speech helped shift American public opinion toward supporting the Allies before U.S. entry into World War II and influenced postwar human rights thinking, including the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

events.title: U.S. Capitol Attack
events.description: A mob of supporters of President Donald Trump stormed the United States Capitol in Washington, D.C., disrupting the joint session of Congress that was certifying the results of the 2020 presidential election.
events.significance: The attack was a major breach of the peaceful transfer of power in the United States, leading to a second impeachment of Trump, numerous prosecutions, and ongoing debate about American democracy.
